section.title: Working with profiles
section.para: Configuration profiles are key for unattended installation and to perform advanced configuration of Agama. However, getting your profile right is not always easy.
Fortunatelly, Agama’s command-line interface offers several commands to validate, load and export configurations, becoming a very valuable tool for writing and debugging your profile.

section.title: Manually loading a profile
section.para: An Agama profile is written in Jsonnet, which is a superset of JSON. It means that any valid JSON file is a valid Jsonnet file too.

However, a profile (either Jsonnet or JSON) should be converted to plain JSON before it is processed by Agama internals. For that reason, we might consider that loading a profile is a three steps process:

listitem.para: Fetch the profile from the given URL.
Evaluate the Jsonnet code to generate the final JSON file. If you are using files or scripts, any relative URL will be resolved in this stage. It will use the URL of the profile as the base URL.
Load the JSON file into the Agama service.

section.para: The whole process is automatically performed by Agama when inst.auto is used. Internally, the mentioned steps are handled by the agama config generate (steps 1 and 2) and agama config load (step 3) subcommands. Thus, the process can be replicated manually.
section.programlisting: $ agama config generate http://example.lan/agama.jsonnet > agama.json $ agama config load < agama.json
section.para: Or if you prefer, you can use this one-liner:
section.programlisting: $ agama config generate http://example.lan/agama.jsonnet | agama config load
section.para: :::tip agama config load does not start the installation

The agama config load just loads the configuration but it does not start the installation. You can use the web user interface to check that everything looks as you expect. If you want to start the installation from the command-line, you can issue the agama install command.

If you are using relative URLs (for instance, within the files or the scripts section), the agama config load might not work as you expect. As agama config load only receives a piece of JSON, it does not know which is the base URL and it will use, as a fallback, the path to the working directory (the one where you are executing the command from). For that reason, it is usually a good idea to pre-process the profile using the agama config generate command.

section.title: Validating a profile
section.para: Agama relies on JSON Schema for profiles validation. The easiest way is to use Agama’s command-line tool.
Bear in mind that you can only validate JSON profiles, not Jsonnet ones. So if you have a Jsonnet file, you need to convert it to JSON using the agama config generate subcommand.
section.programlisting: $ agama config generate my-profile.jsonnet > my-profile.json $ agama config validate my-profile.json
section.para: All of the agama config subcommands validate the profile automatically.
If you do not have a running instance of Agama, you can perform a local validation adding the --local switch.
Alternatively, you can use any JSON Schema validator using the schemas shipped in the agama-common package.
